We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a tolyl (para?) ring with sulfonamide linking to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline.

Structure: p-methyl phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH? Wait: The amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl with an NH (aniline) at the other side? Actually C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: amide carbonyl attached to aniline (anilide) with an NH on phenyl (aniline). So final product has three fragments: tolyl sulfonyl phenyl (sulfonamide), the phenyl attached to unsaturated chain, and an aniline.

We need 3 reactions: likely (1) sulfonamide formation between tolyl amine and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl phenyl (maybe from sulfonyl chloride). (2) amide coupling between carboxylic acid (from α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline. (3) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide bond: gives acid fragment: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait need acid: the α,β-unsaturated acid precursor: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) attached to sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the sulfonamide attaches to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which also bears the unsaturated acid side chain. So after breaking amide, we get precursor A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1 (the acid). Precursor B: aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then step 2: amide coupling.

Next, break the C=C double bond formation via Doebner: precursor A derived from aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) attached to sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the aldehyde is on same phenyl ring as sulfonamide. So we need aldehyde precursor: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1. Then Doebner with malonic acid gives α,β-unsaturated acid.

Third step: sulfonamide formation: combine tolyl amine (p-toluidine) Cc1ccc(N)cc1 with sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl phenyl (maybe 4-sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl group attached to phenyl ring: NS(=O)(=O)c2... So sulfonyl chloride would be ClSO2-Ph? Wait sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl: ClSO2-c2ccc(... )? The sulfonyl chloride reacting with tolyl amine gives sulfonamide. So precursor: tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-c2ccc(CHO)cc2) (the phenyl sulfonyl chloride). After step 2 (Doebner) we have the phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually Doebner gives acid, not chloride. So we need sulfonyl chloride earlier, then after sulfonamide formation we have sulfonamide with aldehyde, then Doebner to convert aldehyde to unsaturated acid, then amide coupling.

Thus three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CHO). 2) Doebner modification on the aldehyde of sulfonamide to give α,β-unsaturated acid (still sulfonamide). 3) amide coupling with aniline to give final product.

We need to provide JSON with three reaction nodes nested.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We need to search for templates matching these transformations.

First, sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_formed: ["sulfonamides"]; broken: maybe "alkyl halide"? Actually sulfonyl chloride is a sulfonyl halide. Use functional_groups_broken: ["alkyl halide"]? Not sure. Let's search with functional_groups_formed sulfonamides and broken alkyl halide.
